text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The World Jewish Restitution Organisation (WJRO) will use all available means to block NATO accession by Poland, the Czech Republic and Romania if these countries do not return the property of Jewish religious communities, WJRO president Naphtali Lavie said.
ZYCIE

- Poland's former prime minister and leader of the opposition centrist Union for Freedom, Tadeusz Mazowiecki, will not run for parliament in the September elections but will canvass for the party in the campaign, Mazowiecki said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Bank Handlowy has received a full operating licence from Russia's central bank. The state-owned Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ), the agricultural sector bank, was awarded a preliminary permit to open a branch in the country and Bank Wschodnioeuropejski has applied for a similar licence.
- Poland's wholesale sales in April grew by 3.9 percent on March and by 42.3 percent compared with the same period last year, a report by the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- Zygmunt Solorz, the co-owner of Polsat television wants to form a financial consortium to buy the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard. The details of the scheme will be known by the end of June, Solorz said.

- The Sobieslaw Zasada Centrum (SZC) automotive group has made an advance payment of 7.5 million zlotys under the planned share capital increase of up to 30.5 million zlotys in the Star truck maker in Starachowice, south Poland, Star's President Roman Musial said.
- The market value of the KGHM copper conglomerate, slated for privatisation this year, ranges between $1.0 billion and $1.3 billion, an analysis by the Creditanstalt Investment Bank (CIB) said.

- BIG-Bank Gdanski, to be formed through the fusion of the listed Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych (BIG) and Bank Gdanski, will focus of retail banking services development, BIG president Boguslaw Kott said.

- The Filar SA insurance firm in Szczecin plans to increase share capital by up to 12 million zlotys, showing growth of up 60 percent, through a closed share issue, Filar's deputy president Janusz Ziejewski said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- The cities of Warsaw, Gdansk, Katowice, Krakow, Poznan, Szczecin and Wroclaw are Poland's most attractive investment centres, a survey by the Gdansk Market Economy Research Institute said.
- Around 25 percent of Poles support the present rate of the economy's privatisation, 33 percent would speed it up and 18 percent want a slowdown, a survey by the CBOS polling institute said.
- Information requirements faced by firms seeking a share listing on the regulated over-the-counter (OTC) market should be less demanding, the OTC president Czeslaw Gawlowski said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The KFKS foundation for mass communications, which holds 60 percent of the RMF FM broadcaster, wants to buy immediately a 40 percent stake in the broadcaster controlled by Bank Przemyslowo Handlowy (BPH), the KFKS and RMF president Stanislaw Tyczynski said.

- The SZC automotive group plans to block the share issue by the Star truck maker addressed to a financial consortium led by Polski Bank Rozwoju (PBR) Polish Development Bank at the general shareholders meeting tomorrow, SZC's spokesperson Marcin Trzaska said.
PARKIET
- Salomon Brothers expects Poland's credit rating to rise to BBB in the next two years, a May 28 report by the bank said.
- The Trzebionka zinc mine, controlled by the Hetman National Investment Fund (NFI), will make a gross profit of between 10 million and 20 million zlotys, NFI Hetman said.
NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
